newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador wants to renegotiate Paris Club debt.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador wants to renegotiate Paris Club debt.

text.p: The president of Ecuador's policy-setting Monetary Board, Danilo Carrera, said Friday the government will ask for a renegotiation of the country's Paris Club debt.
"What is renegotiable (of Ecuador's foreign debt) is what is called the Paris Club debt. This will be renegotiated," Carrera told journalists.
Of Ecuador's total $14.5 billion foreign debt, some $2.0 billion is Paris Club debt.
According to official figures, Ecuador is $200 million in arrears on its Paris Club debt.
Finance Minister Carlos Davalos confirmed Carrera's statements.
"The debt that we can renegotiate we intend to renegotiate," Davalos told reporters.

Carrera explained that the commercial debt renegotiated in 1994 cannot be reviewed. That also applies to debt with the World Bank, the Inter-American Development Bank and the Andean Development Corporation.
The statements by Carrera came after a meeting with President Fabian Alarcon in which they discussed various economic measures to be announced next week.
Alarcon has insisted his new administration will respect Ecuador's debt and international commitments.
The servicing of the country's foreign debt will take up some 45 percent of this year's budget, according to official figures.
